newsitem.title: UK: BP tracks crude higher after OPEC quota pact.
newsitem.headline: BP tracks crude higher after OPEC quota pact.

text.p: British oil shares rallied on Thursday, tracking a firmer crude price, after OPEC's agreement overnight to commit to quotas and cut back production, dealers and analysts said.
At 0813 GMT, shares in British Petroleum Co Plc were up 13-1/2p to 728, while Shell Transport firmed 5p to 1244p.
Among oil exploration companies, shares in Enterprise Oil Plc advanced 10-1/2p to 680 and Cairn Energy Plc rose 7-1/2p to 502-1/2.
OPEC members agreed to extend a freeze on the cartel's production quotas until the end of the year and the majority of the 11 members who cheat on quotas vowed to stop.
"If you believe that, then oil prices look good for now and will continue to look good to the end of the year," said an oil sector special salesman.
SIMEX brent was quoted at $18.14 a barrel.
Analyst David Stedman of DAIWA Europe noted a recent rotation out of oil stocks and said the conclusion of the OPEC meeting has provided the impetus for investors to get back in the sector.
But it remains to be seen whether oil stocks can sustain a rally if oil prices slip back, he added.
In a research note, Lehman Brothers said it was maintaining its 1997 forecast for average oil prices of $19.00 per barrel.

Commenting on the meeting, Lehman said: "OPEC has never previously made such a statement on quota busters - we remain somewhat sceptical that it will happen to this degree by year end. However, the short-term impact on oil prices and sentiment is very positive."
